title: The wedding date is written
hook: Sohila's first hymn speaks of death as a wedding day already fixed, asking friends for blessing (Gauri Deepaki, ang 12)

segments.voice: Yesterday, birha, the ache of separation; your line was longing is love too. Today, the bride again, and the day her waiting ends.

Before an old Punjabi wedding, the date is fixed and written down. Friends crowd around the bride with blessings, and in the custom the hymn draws on, a little oil is poured at the threshold. Everyone knows the day is coming. Sikhs sing a hymn at bedtime that uses exactly this picture. And the wedding it's talking about is not the one you'd expect.
screen: `THE DATE IS FIXED, WRITTEN.` → `FRIENDS BRING BLESSINGS.` → `OIL AT THE THRESHOLD.`

segments.voice: Kirtan Sohila is the Sikh night prayer, short hymns sung before sleep. It's also sung at the end of a Sikh funeral. Its first hymn is by Guru Nanak, in Rag Gauri Deepaki, on Ang 12, and its central line, in the original, is this: sanbat saahaa likhiaa mil kar paavahu tel. The year and the day are written; come together, friends, and pour the oil. Then: give me your blessings, so that I may meet my Lord. The bride is the soul. The groom is God. And the wedding day, fixed and written, is the day of death. It sounds heavy. It isn't meant to be. The hymn doesn't threaten, and it doesn't describe punishments. It turns death into a homecoming, the day the long-waiting bride from two days ago finally goes to her beloved. It adds that this summons comes to every house, every day, and so it asks us to remember the One who calls. Some readers hear why it belongs at night: sleep is a small rehearsal of letting go. You lie down not knowing, trusting the morning. At a funeral, the same words tell the family: this was not an ambush. It was a date, written, and a wedding. And the hymn is honest about its limit: it doesn't say when anyone's day is. Only that it's written, and that the wise way to live is to remember it gently, with friends and blessing.
screen: `KIRTAN SOHILA — THE NIGHT PRAYER.` · `SANBAT SAAHAA — THE DATE IS SET.` · `DEATH AS A WEDDING, NOT A THREAT.` · `EVERY NIGHT, A SMALL LETTING GO.` · then, large: `THE DATE IS WRITTEN.`

segments.voice: Let yourself remember, calmly, that your days are counted, as everyone's are; not to frighten yourself, just to see today clearly. Think of one thing you'd want to have done or said if you knew the date, a thank-you, an apology, a call, and hold it lightly. Let the breath be slow, the way it is before sleep.
Saahaa, the fixed wedding date. From Kirtan Sohila's first hymn: death pictured as the soul's wedding day, already fixed, met with friends and blessing rather than fear.
Your line: the date is written. Death as a homecoming, not a threat. Gently, until tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 246 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: FROM WOMAN WE ARE BORN.`

howItsDone: Many Sikhs recite or sing Kirtan Sohila before sleep each night, and it is also recited when the Guru Granth Sahib is closed for the night and at the end of a Sikh funeral.
